Where it began

Andy Flower was born in Cape Town on 28 April 1968 and went to school at Oriel Boys' High and then Vainona High. From his schooldays on, much of his cricket was played next to his younger brother Grant, and the two of them went on to share a dressing room for Zimbabwe for years.

His first international match was a one-day game against Sri Lanka at New Plymouth, in the 1992 World Cup. He made a hundred in it, the first man to manage that on his one-day debut at a World Cup.

The player

He played 63 Tests for Zimbabwe between 1992 and 2002, scoring 4,794 runs at 51.55 with 12 hundreds and 27 fifties. His best, 232 not out, was by 2026 the highest Test innings ever played by a wicketkeeper. Behind the stumps he took 142 catches and made nine stumpings, and he led his country in 20 Tests.

India saw him at his finest in a 2000/01 series: 550 runs in four innings, and he was out only twice. Late in 2001 he was ranked the best Test batsman in the world, and by 2026 he held Zimbabwe's records for most Test runs and the highest Test average.

What made him special

For most sides a wicketkeeper's runs are a bonus. For Zimbabwe, his were the backbone of the batting. He played spin superbly, and by 2026 no other keeper had finished a Test career averaging fifty.

His one-day career had one quirk a friend might tease him about. After that debut hundred he waited until his 150th match for his second, a record for patience nobody seems in a hurry to beat.

Away from the middle

After a season with Essex and another with South Australia he turned to coaching. He joined England as assistant coach in 2007 and became team director in 2009. In his time England won the Ashes at home in 2009, the World Twenty20 in 2010 and the Ashes in Australia that winter, and in August 2011 they became the top-ranked Test side. He was made an OBE, named Wisden Cricketer of the Year, and was the BBC's Coach of the Year in 2011.

In 2021 he became the first Zimbabwean in the ICC Hall of Fame. He coached Royal Challengers Bengaluru to their first IPL title in 2025 and another in 2026.

And finally

He bowled in Tests without taking a wicket, which may be why he kept the gloves on. It hardly mattered: the runs he made with the bat were more than enough for one man.
